_comment: The one truth for the A3 system's OSC vocabulary, ports, IPs and network.
Decided on 2026-09-30: every program reads this file (a3_osc.py for Python),
or is rendered from it at install, and nothing else carries these facts.
The register (a3-core tools/tests) fails on any address, port or IP literal
found outside it. Change a fact here and every device follows.
network: what the a3-core package configures (systemd-networkd).
hosts: every machine by name.
listeners: who listens where -- program, role, host, port.
routes: who sends to which listener. carries: vu marks the meters going to a
port that is not a vu listener (the mixer takes them on its OSC port).
addresses: our vocabulary. {ch} counts 1..4, {n} counts 1..40.
args: the type on the wire. Core announces switches and lamps as floats (0.0/1.0) and
reads every value with float(), so the mixer's values, sent as text, count too. f|s:
the filter mode arrives as a name from the desk (high_pass) and a number from Motion.
relayed_to: Core passes an arrival on to these, the sender left out.
announced_to: Core says it itself, to everybody, the sender too -- a lamp
is status, so the desk's lamp follows the desk's own key.
external: vocabularies we speak but do not own (REAPER, the IEM plug-ins).
meters: how every display moves a meter bar (decided 2026-10-07). The sources
send raw peaks; each display applies these on its own clock: attack (0 =
at once), release in dB per second, and how long the highest peak is held.

listeners.name: core.osc
listeners.carries: every controller's messages, and /beat from the analyzer

listeners.name: core.reaper-feedback
listeners.carries: REAPER's own OSC feedback

listeners.name: core.vu-relay
listeners.carries: the analyzer's and StemDeck's /vu bundles, forwarded unchanged to the remote Motion followed and to every desk followed (the analyzer needs OSC_VU_core=127.0.0.1:9003; Core renders it into the analyzer's conf.d, 50-a3-osc.env)

listeners.name: core.web
listeners.carries: the traffic window (HTTP, not OSC); every interface, decided 2026-09-30

listeners.name: motion.osc
listeners.carries: Core's relays (StemDeck's preview among them), /beat

listeners.name: motion.vu
listeners.carries: the analyzer's /vu bundles

listeners.name: motion.energy
listeners.carries: the IEM EnergyVisualizer's /EnergyVisualizer/RMS

listeners.name: stemdeck.osc
listeners.carries: Core's bus switches and its request for all of them; a one-deck instance k (--deck A..D) listens on this port + (k - 1): A 7780, B 7781, C 7782, D 7783 (Core's deck relay sends deck k there); the two-deck StemDeck keeps 7780

listeners.name: devices.announce
listeners.carries: Core's /core/here broadcast: where every device fetches the truth

listeners.name: mixer.osc
listeners.carries: Core's relays and lamps, /beat, /vu

listeners.name: desk.osc
listeners.carries: Core's relays, lamps and stems, /beat -- every virtual desk Core follows (four at most)

listeners.name: desk.vu
listeners.carries: the analyzer's and StemDeck's /vu bundles, forwarded unchanged by Core (core.vu-relay)

listeners.name: beat-analyzer.clock
listeners.carries: /tap, /clockmode, and /beat from Motion in clock mode 0

listeners.name: reaper.osc
listeners.carries: Core's /track/... control

listeners.name: iem.multiencoder-1
listeners.carries: /MultiEncoder/... (receiver set inside the plug-in, in the REAPER project)

listeners.name: iem.multiencoder-2
listeners.carries: /MultiEncoder/... (receiver set inside the plug-in, in the REAPER project)

listeners.name: iem.multiencoder-3
listeners.carries: /MultiEncoder/... (receiver set inside the plug-in, in the REAPER project)

listeners.name: dualdelay.osc
listeners.carries: /DualDelay/delayBPML|R (receiver set inside the plug-in, in the REAPER project)

listeners.name: engine.osc
listeners.carries: a3-engine: Core's words in engine mode -- channel.gain/eq.*/volume/3d/filter.frequency/filter.q/aux-send/cue/filter/azimuth/elevation/source, filter.frequency/resonance/mode, master.*, aux-return.source/cue, delay.bpm, engine.open

listeners.name: x11vnc.vnc
listeners.carries: the Core's screen (VNC, not OSC)

listeners.name: screencast.stream
listeners.carries: the screen's picture as MPEG-TS, several viewers on one encode (OBS, the pro-DJ apps) (listener, not OSC)

listeners.name: radla.osc
listeners.carries: /beat

listeners.name: radla.vu
listeners.carries: /vu

listeners.name: prolink.announce
listeners.carries: Pro DJ Link keep-alives (broadcast, not OSC)

listeners.name: prolink.beat
listeners.carries: Pro DJ Link beat packets (broadcast, not OSC)

listeners.name: prolink.status
listeners.carries: Pro DJ Link status packets (broadcast, not OSC)

listeners.name: aes67.stream
listeners.carries: the Core's 12 channels as AES67 (RTP, L24, 44.1 kHz, 0.5 ms packets), multicast on the audio socket; not OSC

listeners.name: aes67.sap
listeners.carries: AES67 stream announcements (SAP/SDP), multicast on the audio socket, every sender and receiver; not OSC

listeners.name: ptp4l.event
listeners.carries: PTP event messages; the Core is master on the audio socket; not OSC

listeners.name: ptp4l.general
listeners.carries: PTP general messages (announce, follow-up); not OSC

channel.aux-send.meaning: send to the FX bus (the beat-synced DualDelay)

channel.cue.meaning: cue the channel to the headphones (its pre-fader send to enc_phones); was pfl until 2026-10-01

channel.filter.meaning: this channel through the master filter

channel.filter.frequency.meaning: the channel's own filter cutoff (was pot_1)

channel.filter.q.meaning: the channel's own filter Q (was pot_2)

channel.3d.meaning: how much of the channel's isolated band moves, as an amplitude 0..1; the steady rest never changes

channel.azimuth.meaning: the channel's direction, degrees; live only to the pro-DJ apps followed; a recall replays the last one to everyone, as before

channel.elevation.meaning: the channel's height, degrees; live only to the pro-DJ apps followed; a recall replays the last one to everyone, as before

channel.stem.turn.meaning: the channel's encoder turned by this many clicks (signed): moves its selector's cursor over the channel's three positions in a ring -- on channel N: deck 1's stem N, deck 2's stem N, then A, the analog input; left from deck 1's stem N is A; switches nothing

channel.stem.meaning: what the channel plays: while its source is STEM, the stems on its bus as a bit mask of pairs 1-8 (bit 0 = pair 1 = deck A stem 1); 0 = the analog input, sent whenever its source is ANALOG, whatever is on its bus; on channel N only bit N-1 (deck 1's stem N) or bit N+3 (deck 2's stem N)

channel.stem.push.meaning: the channel's encoder pushed: on A, the channel's source becomes ANALOG -- REAPER opens its analog send and shuts its stems send, StemDeck is not asked and the stem on its bus stays there, unheard; on a stem (deck 1's or deck 2's stem N on channel N), the source becomes STEM and the stem the channel's only input -- the other deck's stem N goes to the return (AUX); on the stem already on its bus nothing moves; without StemDeck a stem push switches nothing, A still does

channel.stem.cursor.meaning: the channel's selector cursor: on channel N one of N-1 (deck 1's stem N), N+3 (deck 2's stem N) and 8 = A, the analog input; a stored cursor outside these comes back as 8

filter.led.meaning: the filter section's lamp: blue HPF, green LPF (was /fx/led)

master.aux-return.meaning: the aux return, the fifth stereo input (was /master/return)

aux-return.stem.turn.meaning: the aux return's encoder turned by this many clicks (signed): moves its cursor in a ring along the display, STEM (1) -> ANALOG (0) -> CUE (2) -> STEM; switches nothing

aux-return.stem.push.meaning: the aux return's encoder pushed: switches the return to the mode under the cursor; on CUE it toggles the return's cue and switches no mode

aux-return.stem.meaning: the aux return's cursor (0 = analog, 1 = stem, 2 = cue), then pairs 1-8: 1 = on StemDeck's AUX bus, i.e. on no channel (heard on the return in stem mode only)

aux-return.stem.mode.meaning: the aux return's mode, which chooses its source: 1 = stem (StemDeck's AUX bus plays on the return; analog 11/12 is shut), 0 = analog (analog inputs 11/12 play on the return; StemDeck's AUX is shut). Never both. In either mode every stem on no channel is on StemDeck's AUX

channel.source.meaning: the channel's source in engine mode: 0 = analog, k = deck k (1 = A, 2 = B); from Core's deck selector, to the engine as its switch and to the desk and Motion as the channel-source report

channel.source.cursor.meaning: engine mode: the channel's selector cursor over its ring, 0 = analog, k = deck k (1 = A, 2 = B); moves on channel.stem.turn, becomes the source on channel.stem.push

aux-return.source.meaning: the aux return's source in engine mode: 0 = analog 11/12, k = deck k's AUX pair; never both

aux-return.cue.meaning: the aux return's cue in engine mode, 1 = on, 0 = off

delay.bpm.meaning: the delay's tempo for both lines in engine mode, 20-400 (Core's tempo follower)

engine.open.meaning: 1 opens main, booth and phones (a 1 s ramp to the calibrated level), 0 closes them

engine.hello.meaning: the engine's boot id, every 2 s; a new id makes Core replay its state and open the outputs

stemdeck.3d.meaning: deck k's 3D, 0-1: the desk's 3D of the channel holding deck k, 1 (neutral) while it is on no channel

stemdeck.present.meaning: 1 while deck k's hello is fresh (5 s at most), else 0

stemdeck.deck-hello.meaning: a StemDeck instance names the deck it plays (host), at start and every 2 s; device.hello carries no deck number

aux-return.cue.led.meaning: the aux return's cue lamp, 1 = on

stemdeck.bus.meaning: set one bus switch of a stem, 1 on 0 off; bus 1-4 the desk channels, 5 AUX (StemDeck's own cue bus 6 is gone since 2026-10-07: a channel is cued through its own bus); stem N reaches only bus N and 5 (AUX): StemDeck and Core refuse a switch onto another bus

stemdeck.buses.meaning: a stem's bus switches as a bit mask (bit 0 = bus 1), after every change and for all 8 stems after /stemdeck/recall

stemdeck.recall.meaning: report every stem's buses once; Core asks when StemDeck's hello is news

stemdeck.ahead.meaning: StemDeck's preview of the music on the audible deck (the MASTER deck when both are heard): the current bar's section (groove, build, drop, breakdown; none: no deck is heard, or it is not analysed yet), the next section (end: no change before the set ends), the bars until it (-1: a loop turns back before it) and the bar's energy 0-1 against the set's loud bars. On every downbeat and on a load, jump, loop, pitch or deck change; Core passes it on to the Motion it follows, unchanged, and never replays it

device.hello.meaning: a device names itself and the sha256 of its copy of this file, at start and every 30 s; Core's window shows whether it is Core's own. Core follows the StemDeck and the Motion that arrived last (one of each), a remote Motion instead of the rig's own, and forgets one silent for a minute; and every desk (the A³ Mixer on a screen) that says hello with Core's own truth, four at most, each until it has been silent for a minute; a pro-DJ app says `prodj` and is followed as a desk of that kind

core.here.meaning: Core, every 2 s by broadcast: the URL of the joined truth, its fingerprint (sha256 of the canonical JSON) and a boot id, a random token that is new with every Core start (a changed boot id means a new Core, even one restarted within seconds); readers also accept the older two-string form

state.recall.meaning: say the state again; the answer is the ordinary messages

prodj.live.meaning: the single global pro-DJ LIVE state, 1 = a pro-DJ app may operate. Core holds it, starts off, and repeats it every 5 s while on; a device counts it off 12 s after the last 1. Motion only ever sends 0

stemdeck.pointer.meaning: a click on StemDeck's screen picture: phase 0 down, 1 move, 2 up; x, y a share of the screen from top-left; forwarded only while pro-DJ LIVE

motion.pointer.meaning: a click on Motion's screen picture: phase 0 down, 1 move, 2 up; x, y a share of the screen from top-left; forwarded only while pro-DJ LIVE

core.device-at.meaning: where a followed device runs: device (motion, stemdeck) and host. Sent to a pro-DJ app when it joins or recalls, and when that device moves

beat.meaning: beat in bar, bar, tempo -- the clock (Motion sends it only in clock mode 0)

vu.meaning: peak, rms (linear) of VU channel n. REAPER out per range: 1-20 = out n + 30, 21-36 = out n - 10, 51-66 = out n; 41-50 come from StemDeck, 9-10 and 37-40 are free. 1-8 analog1_L ... analog4_R the four channels' analog inputs, L and R each (REAPER track "analog" = system:capture_1-8, before any channel processing, shown under the desk's A even while a stem plays); 11-20 main_sub, main_top1 ... main_top9 the main outputs; 21-30 booth_sub, booth_top1 ... booth_top9 the booth outputs; 31-34 phones_L, phones_R, rec_L, rec_R the phones and the recording bus; 35-36 aux_L, aux_R the return's analog input, L and R (REAPER track "analog" channels 11-12 = system:capture_11-12, shown under the return's ANALOG whatever the return plays); 41-48 StemDeck's stems, one each (stem_a1 ... stem_b4: peak of the louder side, rms over both, as the stem leaves StemDeck on a bus: after knob, mute, deck fader and the bus trim -- so a stem alone on a channel reads as that channel's in{n}_pre; a stem on no bus shows what it would send); 49-50 StemDeck's AUX bus, L and R: peak and rms of each side after the bus; 51-66 the channels in stereo, L and R each: 51-58 in1_pre_L ... in4_pre_R (input after TRIM/EQ, post-fader), 59-66 in1_post_L ... in4_post_R (channel bus post-fader, moving + steady); see vu_meters. A remote Motion gets the analyzer's from Core (core.vu-relay), unchanged
